decided_by: approved with 1 advisory objection(s) — none high-severity

objections.problem: Test sketch only shows two assertions (prefix-based reach predicate, duplicate detection) but claims 14 fixtures and 4 mutation runs; the fixture table and mutation results aren't shown, so distinctness/reach coverage across all 18 arms can't be independently confirmed from the plan text alone.

reviews.notes: Edits are additive and land on the causal path the rationale names: the shared struct (edit 1) plus recordedArm (edit 2) close the 'uninstrumented revalidator looks like unreached rung' conflation explicitly, and the 18 named constants at their return sites (edit 3) are exactly the mechanism the diagnosis says a refusal counter cannot replace — a gate_ prefix that is queryable distinguishes 'reached' from 'refused' without adding new counters or predicates. No edit branches on the new field, matching the stated invariant. Scope is minimal: no unrelated files touched, no renaming of existing arms, no new counters added to the sweep report. The four-revalidator gap is explicitly flagged in risks with the naming convention (unreported:<item_type>) that prevents it reading as absence, and tracked separately (features_open/032) rather than silently expanded into this change's scope, which is correct minimality.

missing: Whether the shared-revalidator-arm work referenced as features_open/032 was itself checked against for overlap before this plan proceeded with instrumenting only one revalidator first.
reviews.notes: This is additive instrumentation on an existing struct/action, not a new agent/table/migration — low reuse risk by nature. The plan explicitly scopes itself to one revalidator and tracks extending the other four as separate work (features_open/032) rather than silently duplicating a pattern across files, which is the right discipline. My only soft concern: the plan does not show evidence of having searched for an existing generic 'which rung fired' pattern elsewhere on the platform (e.g. diagnosis loop's own ladder-style gates) before inventing recordedArm/arm vocabulary locally — worth a cheap check but not blocking given the small blast radius and explicit non-behavioural constraint.

objections.problem: revalidationVerdict is the shared record type returned by all five review-queue revalidators (voice_tells, needs_page, and others per the plan's own risk note), not just claims_unverified. Adding a field to it is low-risk (json omitempty), but the plan should confirm no revalidator serializes/compares this struct against a fixed schema or golden fixture downstream.

reviews.notes: Contained to two action files plus one shared struct in the review-queue revalidation subsystem — not core dispatch/orchestrator/messaging, so stability preference doesn't bind here. Field is additive (omitempty), no predicate or branch changes, matches the author's own stated invariant. Partial population across revalidators is acknowledged and self-describing (unreported:<item_type> sentinel) rather than silently misleading. Test plan drives real fixtures and checks for duplicate/mis-prefixed arm names, which is the right failure mode to guard given this becomes a queried vocabulary. No objection rises above low; approving.

This plan touches the claims_unverified revalidator (platform/orchestration/actions/revalidate_review_queue_action.go and revalidate_unverified_claims.go), not the 090 diagnosis loop. No changes to verdict citation tiers, read-only SQL guard layers, diagnosis_artifacts/notes persistence, error_step config placement, or pod/token isolation. The added `arm` field is additive JSON instrumentation on a work-item revalidation record, explicitly stated to add no branching logic. Out of scope for this seat; approve.

Pure instrumentation on the claims_unverified revalidator: adds an observation-only `arm` string to result.revalidation, no predicate/ladder/order changes, nothing branches on the new field. Does not generate, alter, or weaken any user-facing claim, gate, scanner, or banned-claim list; does not touch prompts/specs/writing rules; no legal-page or disclaimer surface involved. The plan is explicit that this makes gate reachability observable, not that any gate now approves more or fewer items, and the risk section correctly refuses to overclaim what the change accomplishes. No overclaimed-reliability or poisoned-spec surface here.

objections.problem: The plan's whole justification is 'the question becomes a GROUP BY instead of a prose match' over result.revalidation.arm — but the landmine list names this exact file and field shape twice: 'resolution_path=\'auto:revalidated\' / revalidate_unverified_claims.go — A per-row revalidation stamp is LAST-WRITE-WINS, so GROUP BY it reads exactly like a run log and is not one.' Each item's result.revalidation is overwritten on every sweep, so GROUP BY arm over site_work_items answers 'what did the latest run decide per item', not 'how often is each rung reached over time' — the historical question the rationale implies it now answers. The grounded_in section actually scopes its own example query by a single sweep timestamp (2026-08-13T08:44:39Z), which is the correct pattern, but the general framing overclaims what the new field buys.

No deploy/verification step is specified beyond unit tests. Per house discipline, a code change like this should be confirmed live via the running pod (grep the binary for an arm constant like 'gate_claims_still_present'), not via git or image tag — same-tag rebuilds can ship stale binaries. Worth adding explicitly even though this is low-risk instrumentation.

reviews.notes: No SQL migration or stored-content surgery here, so needle-gate discipline, informational-column blast-radius scoping, and repair-vs-regenerate taxonomy don't directly apply — this is pure Go instrumentation. The one real hit is that the exact per-row revalidation stamp this field lives in already has a documented GROUP BY pitfall on file for this file, and the plan's rationale leans on GROUP BY as the payoff. Not a blocker for the additive/non-branching field itself, but the rationale should be corrected or the query pattern constrained to per-sweep scoping before this is cited as 'now queryable by GROUP BY' in follow-up work.

This is pure additive instrumentation: a new omitempty field, named constants at existing return sites, no reordering/removal of gates, no branching on the new field (explicitly stated and structurally consistent with the sketch). It targets the actual diagnosed cause -- three verdict counters cannot distinguish 'gate refused' from 'gate never reached' -- rather than patching around a symptom; no known bug is being routed past. The uneven population (only one revalidator instrumented) is explicitly stated and justified as deferred work tracked in features_open/032, satisfying the deferral-must-be-stated rule. No new struct/action duplicates existing machinery; recordedArm is a small helper justified by testability, not a reinvention. No SQL changes ship in this plan itself (the grounded_in queries are read-only diagnostic evidence, not part of the edit), so schema-first/parameterised rules aren't engaged by the code changes. No renames: existing field/verdict names are untouched, arm is a genuinely new key. Tone is plain and mechanical throughout. Risks section is honest about a real gap (fleet-wide LIKE 'gate_%' misreading) without hiding it. No objections.

Pure instrumentation on a claims-revalidation ladder: adds an observation-only 'arm' field to record which rung decided a verdict, no predicate/branching/ordering changes, no revenue-shape or classifier-bypass implications. Does not touch site classification, planning, composition, or content generation paths. Mission-neutral.

No absence claim here rests on an unverified premise — the rationale's central fact (gate refusal counters read 0/0/0 while 21 items were decided) is grounded in an actual live query result quoted in grounded_in, not asserted. The plan adds a passive, additive jsonb field with no branching and no new agent/mechanism competing with anything named in the landmines (e.g. it does not touch the ladder's order or predicates). The risks section is honest about partial population and the population-vs-instrumentation distinction. Only open question is whether a similarly-named per-rung tracking field already exists elsewhere in the revalidator family or was proposed/rejected before — hence the precedent and symbol checks, not a blocking concern.

ARCHITECTURE_SIGNAL: point_fix | DEFLECTIONS: unknown

The added field is opt-in (`omitempty`), the unsafe default (absent/empty) is not branched on anywhere, and it is new — no live consumer depends on it yet; the author's own future GROUP BY query is not a dependent consumer today. It sits inside an existing shared struct (`revalidationVerdict`) that is already queried via jsonb path the same way verdict/reason are, so this is not a new contract, just a new labelled column on one that already exists. Blast radius is one package, two source files plus a test; no cross-package symbol, no schema migration, no staged rollout needed.

Forward fitness: the next load is instrumenting the other four revalidators (voice_tells, needs_page, etc. — tracked in features_open/032). This plan's shape — a named-constant enum per return site plus a fallback `unreported:<item_type>` — is a template that generalises cleanly to those, so the design carries the work I can see coming.

Cost of not changing: real and already measured — the 2026-08-13 sweep produced four indistinguishable zero-meanings across the gate counters, discoverable only by LIKE-matching prose. That is a recurring diagnostic tax on every future investigation of this ladder, and the fix is cheap and reversible.

One thing worth tracking but not blocking: the arm vocabulary becomes a queried contract the moment someone writes a dashboard against `gate_%`, and the plan's own risk section already names the accumulation hazard (partial coverage across revalidators) and defers it correctly rather than solving it here.
